Story: I was hauling bricks across the site, sweat stinging my eyes, when I spotted Jamal drifting toward the crane’s shadow. The load above him swayed, a ton of steel and concrete dangling by a thread. Instinct screamed at me—shout, warn him, keep everyone safe. That’s what I’m here for, right? But just as I opened my mouth, my phone buzzed. It was a message from the tenants’ group: the city council was about to pass a policy that would force dozens of families out of their homes, and they needed me to speak up, now, before the vote. My heart hammered. I was the only one on site who could see the danger, but I was also the only advocate the tenants trusted to fight for them. My mind raced—do I yell and break the silence of the site, risking my job for “causing a scene,” or do I grab my phone and try to stop the council, knowing someone’s life might be at stake right here, right now? The weight of both worlds pressed down, and I stood frozen, torn between the urgent demands of the worksite and the desperate pleas of those counting on my voice.
